verdict_note: No blocking finding. The tests that need the build are red for that reason (no view diagram, no view model). Regression R1 is green. The instrument is independent of holon/ and reproduces the committed anchors. Every number I could recompute from committed data matches the key, and both prereg audits and the freeze check pass. The coordinator's extra check finds no I66 change among M3's derivation inputs, so I66's regressions and gate-M3-G2 can both hold. I do not sign off, because three major findings should be folded into the prereg before the key is frozen. M1: I66's code is in every M3 generator closure, so the 123 M3 records that match today's generators go stale. V7, R2 and R3 do not account for this, and FACT's G1 reports stale records. M2: V5 does not say whether builds for a test milestone (gen_milestone maps them to M2), or builds with in-memory diagrams, model the window view; this reaches I24's PAR derivation path and instrument. M3: P1-P4 hold by construction once V2-V5 are implemented, so they should not count as predictions. The ten minor findings concern wording, test strength and scope.

findings.where: tests_m3/test_view_evidence.py:56-61 (V7), :80-87 (V9), :515-517 (R2's never list); spec/M3/predictions.json:2342-2351 (I66-R2, I66-R3); prompts/I66_view_evidence.md:71 ('Closure churn'); holon/fact/gate.py:141-151; holon/sorts/gate3.py:147-222, 225-245, 632-644; holon/undo/run.py:586-624; .github/workflows/holon-ci.yml:118-121; docs/iterations/I26.md:369, 452-453, 496
findings.what:
I66's code changes are holon/gen/targetlib.py (V3), holon/diagram/__init__.py and build.py (V2, V4) and holon/diagram/evidence.py (V5). These files are in every M3 generator closure, not only in the holon-ir/0.2 and 0.3 closures the prereg names. Computed with holon.records._holon_imports at fde1f819: holon.sorts.run3.GEN3 (122 files), GEN3+GEN_FACT (132), GEN3+GEN_UNDO (125) and GEN3+GEN_DISCH (127) each contain holon/gen/targetlib.py and holon/diagram/{__init__,build,evidence,access}.py.
At the base, 123 of the 131 M3 records carry today's digest: 80 PAR (the holon-ir/0.3 closure), 35 DISCH, 5 FACT and 3 typed SORT. The 8 UNDO records are already stale. All 123 go stale when I66's code lands, yet R2 forbids I66 to touch results/M3, and V7 and V9 say no M3 file changes.
Two M3 gate checks see this. FACT's G1 (holon/fact/gate.py, rerun_problems) fails every FACT record whose generator_sha256 is not the FACT digest now. gate3's G1 compares I30's rerun records using norm_record, which removes only 'seconds'.
R3 still says the M3 gate's failing items are the base's, 'I66 adding none', and describes the base's full gate as failing only G11V and G6. That description comes from I26-R4 and was not observed: I26.md:452-453 says TestGate (G1, G6, G11V) was not run, and I26.md:496 lists 'the full M3 gate, including G1' under Not done. By reading gate3.g1, the base's G1 probably fails already: its run names only the I30 laws, holon/undo/run.py then runs no UNDO law, and g1_undo finds no fresh UNDO record for any of the 8.
CI's gate-M3-partial (G3, G5, G8, G9, G10, G11, G11V, GEVID) runs no check that reads generator_sha256, and test_r3 leaves the M3 clause to 'CI and the audits'. I65's build head 12424fcc shows the same: all 131 M3 records are stale there.
findings.why: R3's M3 clause is false in either case. If G1 passes at the base, I66 adds a failing G1. If G1 already fails, the clause describes the base wrongly and hides the new G1 reasons I66 adds. The prompt's 'Closure churn' names M1 and M2 only, so the build report would judge R3 on CI's partial gate alone, while M3's records no longer match their generators, which FACT's own G1 counts as a failure.
findings.fix:
Before freezing, state in V7, R3 and 'Closure churn' that the changed modules are in GEN3, GEN_FACT, GEN_UNDO, GEN_DISCH and the holon-ir/0.3 closure. Then choose one of:
(a) Leave the M3 records stale, as I27's UNDO records are. Restate R3's M3 clause as "CI's gate-M3-partial fails only the base's items; the full gate's G1 gains the FACT staleness and I30 record differences of I66's closure change", and describe the base as it was actually run.
(b) Let I66 re-make the M3 records in generator_sha256 and seconds alone. This needs an R2 exception for results/M3 and matching handling of I43's unregenerated_records pin.
(c) Ask the human. I65 has the same problem.

findings.what: At I66 the view has no ledger bundle, so every 'ledger' value in its diagram is already empty. ledger_free therefore changes only coverage_debt, by dropping the LEDGER debts. The check never sees non-empty links or HASH debt, which is exactly what I65's generated bundle adds (the abstraction's committed diagram, built with its bundle, has ledger links and two HASH debts).
findings.why: The coordination claim rests on this check: I65 moves neither evidence_sha256 nor the registry (I65-R2 allows no registry change except its law's entries). Reading holon/diagram/evidence.py, the claim holds: it reads only a diagram's edges, its carriers' key_space, its predicates and the four identity fields. The test does not show this.
findings.fix: Also run the check on a diagram that has links. For example, ledger_free of gen/M2/diagram/morph_rollup.json must leave morph_rollup's model, atoms and unresolved entries unchanged. Alternatively, graft the abstraction diagram's links and HASH debts onto the view's diagram before the run.

findings.what: For the view's TRANS edges of the two replayed actions (commitBatch, finalizeBatch), I23's coverage writes 'the hand abstraction of X (gen/M2/extracted/m1_view.json, generated by holon.differential: the window view of ... over the hand abstraction, its unmatched requires removed); its extracted counterpart ... was replayed ...'. docs/M2_EXIT.md is an exit deliverable, and it will call a generated view a hand abstraction.
findings.why: This is a false sentence in a committed exit document, accepted as generic wording.
findings.fix: Add a generic case to exit_report for a diagram whose provenance.extraction names a declaration ('the window view of X ...'). R2 already permits this, because only the 11 new entries change. Or record it as a known inaccuracy and a Question.

findings.where: tests_m3/test_view_evidence.py:414-428 (P3: the probe and the derived law); V6 (:50-55)
findings.what: The derived-law check accepts named [] or [TRANS.challengeState] at any time. At I66's end, V6 requires L1-L4 to be unchanged, so the law must name nothing. A build that also carried I65's ghost-L2 rule (e57fa11d) would still pass P3, and also R1, since no prereg law has a ghost term. findings.what: The rest of R2 is judged per own commit. The exit-document clause instead compares results/M2/m2_exit.json at the end commit with the prereg commit. If a lead merged into the PR branch changed m2_exit.json (metrics, refinement records or the instrument), that change would count against I66, as in I65's prereg review finding F5.
findings.why: Another key's merged change could fail I66's own R2.
findings.fix: Judge the clause per own commit against its parent, or state that the PR branch must not merge a lead that changed m2_exit.json.

findings.where: tests_m2/test_evidence.py:584-618; spec/M2/amendments.jsonl (I66's last two I14 lines); tests_m3/test_lean_promoted.py:423-439; spec/M3/amendments.jsonl (last line)
findings.what:
AGENTS rule 2, before and after.
(a) The E3 and E4 inventories now count the fact documents' models only. Before: got = sorted(... for a in atoms(self.doc, 'E3')) and assertTrue(all(a['model'] == ROLLUP for a in atoms(self.doc, 'E3'))). After: e3 = [a for a in atoms(self.doc, 'E3') if a['model'] in DOCS], with the same assertions over e3. E4 changes the same way, with 'if a["model"] in DOCS'. Nothing goes unchecked, because I66-P4 checks the view's 8 E3 and 2 E4 atoms exactly. But after I66 the set holds 17 E3 and 4 E4 atoms, so the words of I14-P5 ('Exactly 9 E3 atoms') and I14-P6 ('Exactly 2 E4 atoms') no longer describe HEAD. The amendment lines say the claims were 'stated over the fact documents' but do not say that their text now reads false, as I65's amendment of I64-R1 did.
(b) Before: assertEqual(file_sha256(root / i['path']), i['sha256']). After: assertEqual(pinned_sha256(root, i['path']), i['sha256']), where pinned_sha256 restores evidence_sha256 to 76c91715... whenever the registry's value equals gen/M2/evidence.json's. This accepts any future change of the evidence set, not only I66's. That is harmless for I43, whose promoted set reads statements only, but it is broader than 'narrowed to I66's outcomes'.
findings.why: Neither change weakens what is checked in substance, but the amendment lines do not state exactly what changed: I14-P5 and I14-P6 now read false at HEAD, and the I43 relaxation reaches beyond I66.
findings.fix: Add to the two I14 lines that the words of I14-P5 and I14-P6 no longer describe HEAD, and say where the view's atoms are checked. Reword the I43 line to say it accepts any evidence_sha256 the committed set holds.

open_questions.question: 1. spec/M3 or spec/M2 as the key's home
open_questions.view: spec/M3 is right. Keys are filed by the phase in which they are preregistered, and I66 is I65's prerequisite, not an M2 exit item. The M3 audit then fingerprints tests_m3/test_view_evidence.py. The cost is the one I65 paid: I14's amendments go in a later commit and are audited by the M2 audit. That is handled.

open_questions.question: 2. The view's diagram in gen/M2/diagram and I23's exit wording
open_questions.view: Listing the view's 11 edges as not replayed is honest: they were not replayed. Calling the view 'the hand abstraction' for commitBatch and finalizeBatch is not. Fix the wording generically (m2) rather than move the view's diagram out of gen/M2/diagram, which would hide it from G1 and from I23's view of the diagrams.

open_questions.question: 3. E5 for window views later
open_questions.view: I agree with deferring it, but V5 should note two consequences. (i) For a REFUTED law over the view whose strongest evidence would be E5, triage flips from finding to intent_question, because the max level becomes E6. (ii) Inheriting the abstraction's assignment is not obviously sound: I13's constraints come partly from the removed requires (tot + n <= qlen, ef + D < t, qpend == btot - bn), so a fresh pass over the view could assign different sorts. The choice is the human's.

open_questions.question: 4. I66 landing the library half of I65's anchor
open_questions.view: The split is coherent. The diagram builder and the evidence pass read libraries only through lib_files and Library.for_facts, never through hints_for. They read the ledger only for links and debt, which the calculus does not read. Two leftovers belong to I65: regress.lib_docs_at and the closure entry for window declarations (m10). The R4 ledger check should exercise links (m1). I65's window_declaration checks neither facts_version nor where the declaration lives, so the rebase must keep V3's narrower condition or amend V3.

open_questions.question: 5. Q62 not in HUMAN_ANSWERS, and no BUILD_PLAN row
open_questions.view: Q62 is not a recorded human answer, so the prompt's 'the human asked' should go or be recorded (m3). Give I66 its BUILD_PLAN row and set the key's plan link to that row before freezing (m4).

open_questions.question: 6. The M1 laws' records over the view stay uncovered
open_questions.view: I agree with leaving them uncovered: covering them needs L1 to match by sha256, which is a calculus change. GEVID does not read results/M2/extracted_m1 at all, so nothing fails. The I66 report should say so.

open_questions.question: 7. Merging the I66 PR with a merge commit
open_questions.view: This is correct and necessary. With a squash or fast-forward merge, I66's commits would become first-parent non-merge commits between I65's prereg and I65's end, and I66's registry change would break I65-R2. I66's own V9 also assumes the PR branch's first-parent chain holds only I66's commits. Merging the lead into the branch is fine, because merge commits are excluded; cherry-picking is not.
